title: Product Profile: Coffee, Tea, Mate and Spices
subtitle: 2025 Edition
org: Kenya Export Promotion and Branding Agency
intro: Kenya's coffee value chain is one of the country's most important economic assets. Coffee is a leading export earner and supports the livelihoods of more than 700,000 smallholder farmers and their families. Kenyan coffee, grown mainly on small farms in the highlands, is highly regarded in international markets for its bright acidity, full body and distinctive fruity and floral notes. The industry also benefits from an established auction system that rewards quality and from long-running relationships with roasters and traders in Europe, Asia and the Americas.

This profile examines Kenya's trade in the coffee, tea, mate and spices family, with particular focus on coffee (HS 0901), Kenya's flagship product in the family. The analysis covers the period 2016 to 2023 and draws on trade values reported to the International Trade Centre (ITC).

Beyond coffee, the family includes tea (HS 0902), Kenya's largest export crop, as well as pepper, vanilla, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg and cardamom, seeds, and ginger, saffron and turmeric. These products give Kenya a diversified agro-processing base and growing opportunities in world markets for speciality and value-added goods.
